title: Tobit and the angel
hookLine: in a book kept in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, young Tobias travels with a stranger who is Raphael

lines: A STRANGER WHO KNOWS THE ROAD.
cards: A young man needs a guide for a long trip, and the first person he meets is a friendly stranger who knows the road. They agree on a wage. The young man's mother cries as they leave, and the family dog trots along behind.
That's the start of a journey in the book of Tobit. Catholic and Orthodox Christians count Tobit among the books of the Bible.

Protestant churches don't count it as scripture, and some Protestant Bibles print it in a separate section called the Apocrypha. So depending on whose Bible is on the shelf, it's either there or it isn't.

teach.h: A BLIND MAN AND A GRIEVING BRIDE.
teach.b: Tobit is an Israelite in exile in Nineveh, a man who gives to the poor and, at real risk, buries the bodies of his people left in the street.

One night he sleeps outside by a wall, sparrow droppings fall into his eyes, and he goes blind. Worn out and humiliated, he prays to die. The same day, far away, a young woman named Sarah prays the same thing.
She's been married seven times, the story says, and each husband was killed by a demon on the wedding night.
Two prayers of despair, and the book says both were heard, and the angel Raphael was sent to heal them both.
Tobit, thinking he's near the end, sends his son Tobias to collect money he once left in trust with a man named Gabael.
The guide Tobias hires says his name is Azarias. Along the road a great fish leaps out of the river at Tobias, and the guide tells him to keep its heart, liver and gall.
Those drive the demon away from Sarah, whom Tobias marries, and heal Tobit's eyes back home.

Only at the end, when the family tries to pay, does the guide say who he is: Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who stand before God. He was there, he says, when Tobit prayed and when he buried the dead.
The help didn't arrive with wings. It walked the same dusty road as a hired companion, and nobody knew until the trip was over.

how: Catholic and Orthodox Christians read Tobit as scripture, and Catholics honor Raphael as an archangel with a feast day; Tobit is sometimes read at Catholic weddings. Protestant churches don't count it as scripture, though some Protestants read it among the Apocrypha.

s: Tobit is in every Christian Bible
Catholic and Orthodox Christians count it as scripture; Protestant churches don't, and some Protestant Bibles print it in the Apocrypha.
the angel tells Tobias who he is at the start of the trip
he calls himself Azarias, and only reveals he's Raphael at the end.
Tobit and Sarah pray on the same day
two prayers of despair in two cities, and Raphael is sent to heal them both.

games.q: you're Tobias, about to set off on a long journey to a place you've never been. you've just met a stranger who knows the road. what do you do?
o: go alone to save the money.
send him on the errand without you.
games.why: Tobias hires him, and the dog comes too. the guide is Raphael, and nobody finds out until the journey's done.

practice: Think of a trip in the day ahead, however short, a walk to the shops, a bus ride, a drive to an appointment, and someone who'd otherwise go alone or is nervous about where they're headed.
Picture being good company on that road: matching their pace, carrying a bag, listening more than talking, staying until they arrive.
If you pray, bring that person and that road before God; if you don't, just walk it once in your mind.

wordCard.voice: Raphael. The hired guide on Tobias's long journey, who turns out to be the angel sent to heal blind Tobit and rescue Sarah.

orig.note: Hebrew: Raphael, the angel sent in the book of Tobit to heal both Tobit and Sarah.
